english.title: Fail comply with a periodic notification requirement re a violent offender order / interim order
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being subject to a violent offender order and periodic notification requirements under section 110 of the Criminal Justice and Immigration Act 2008 failed to notify the police of information required by section 108(2) of the Act, namely **(..SPECIFY THE INFORMATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 113(2)(a) and (6) of the Criminal Justice and Immigration Act 2008.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 110(2) of the Criminal Justice and Immigration Act 2008 provides that a "notifiable date" means in relation to the offender, the date of any notification given by the offender under section 108(1), 109(1) or 110(1).

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 113(6) and (7) of the Criminal Justice and Immigration Act 2008 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit of prosecutions:
None.
